Your phone just buzzed. Check it. Nothing? Your brain made that up.
It's called a phantom vibration. Guess first: how many students in one study felt it? Comment a percent.
So why does your brain fake a buzz?
When you're waiting for a message, your brain stays on alert, like a guard dog barking at every leaf.
Then a tiny muscle twitch, or your jeans pressing on your leg...
Scientists think your brain is so tuned in to that buzz, it mistakes other feelings for it.
For some people, just carrying the phone in a different pocket helps.
